messages:
maya: Heads up from forecasting team 10: new model shows a 38% uplift in short interactive sessions for eu-west1 during the next promo spike. We risk higher fragmentation if we keep current binpack defaults.
ops-bot: [alert] node_pool_utilization eu-west1 increased 59% -> 79% over 12h. median_task=14m, p95=1h45m.
jasper: Do we know composition? short vs long? That drives whether FFD or dedicated micro-pools help.
samir: Breakdown: ~72% sessions <6m, 22% mid (6m-1h), 6% long (>1h). So many tiny allocations causing holes.
lee: Current allocator is latency-first (first-fit). Good for p99 interactive but terrible for fragmentation when short jobs dominate.
tanya: Quick suggestion: carve a labeled fast-pool of "micro-slots" (vGPU slices) for sub-6m tasks. Keep long jobs on regular binpack. Also consider an hourly defragmenter to drain and consolidate long tasks.
jasper: Hybrid might be best: fast-path low-latency allocator for <6m, background FFD consolidation for long jobs. Avoid modifying fast-path to keep scheduler latency low.
samir: Also propose per-tenant short-session rate limiter (token-bucket) to avoid noisy-neighbor storms. Decay tokens faster during peaks to throttle bursty tenants.
lee: Prototype hints: pods can set annotation: redwood.inference/slot-class=fast, redwood.inference/max-runtime=360s. Scheduler treats those as micro-slot candidates and retries quickly.
tanya: Cost math: baseline weekly GPU-hours=19,600h. If micro-pool reserved capacity=1,300h/week but reduces fragmentation reclaimed= -3,000h/week, net -1,700h/week saved. But model risk if fast-pool hit-rate low.
ops-bot: [forecast] model variance: +/-30% depending on hit-rate.
jasper: We'll gate rollout on two metrics: frag_score and reclaimed_hours. Frag_score is new: sum(node_free_spans^2)/total_free_slots (lower better). We'll compute cluster and per-tenant frag_score.
samir: Implementation notes: defrag controller will try to co-locate >=2 long tasks onto same nodes when safe, using graceful cordon+drain with hints. Preemption policy: long jobs can opt-in for checkpointing. Non-opt-in long jobs get scheduled into reserved capacity.
lee: Network/IO check: many short sessions are chat-heavy and increase east-west RPCs. Ensure NIC and port ephemeral limits per node not saturated by micro-slots.
tanya: Canary plan: create eu-west1 micro-pool with 120 micro-slots (spread across AZs) for 72h. Metrics: p95 interactive latency, frag_score delta, reclaimed_gpu_hours. Success criteria: reclaimed_weekly_equiv >1,200h and p99 latency improves or stays same.
maya: Ownership: jasper+lee implement scheduler + manifests. samir+maya run canary and monitor. tanya update cost sims and dashboards.
jasper: I'll open PR with scheduler class + defrag controller tomorrow morning. Will include unit tests and rollout flags.
samir: Also add per-tenant short-session admission counters and a circuit breaker: if a tenant exceeds burst threshold, deny fast-path for 10s and route to normal binpack.
lee: Rollout fallback: if fragmentation worsens or SLA breaches, auto-disable fast-pool and scale reserved burst capacity by +10%.
tanya: Add alert: frag_score increase >15% for 2 consecutive 10m windows -> page infra-oncall.
maya: Timeline: design spec today, canary manifests by EOD, deploy tomorrow, monitor 72h, decision within 7 days. Ops-bot set reminder.
ops-bot: [reminder set] will ping #eng-infra in 74h.
maya: Thanks team. If you see regressions tag #incidents and @maya immediately. :thumbsup:
